analysis.title: GS INDUSTRIALS: Results debates, Airbus seasonal rally, PRY positive on the call...
key_insights: Melrose (MTX) fell 2% on weak results. Margins are being blamed, and incoming client feedback shows limited defence. Some worry the cash drivers do not repeat (e.g. military pre-payments). The call is important with the CMD a month away. Civil aftermarket is underperforming all of A&D despite oil down on the day.

Airbus rose 3% and the desk says the stock should do a year-end rally, citing the seasonal pattern and delivery data that mechanically ramps in coming weeks. Pushback: consensus expects about 100 more deliveries, or 11-12% y/y growth, in 2027, a high bar, and guidance is likely to be set more conservatively.

Airbus management said on the call it is 'reasonably comfortable to be somewhere in the 870 plus or minus 20'. Management called P&W engines the 'pacing item' but said nothing has changed to put planned 2027/2028 output at risk. The share buyback announced at the CMD starts between now and year end.

European defence rose 2%. Kongsberg (KOG) beat in Q3 and BAE rebounded on a UK plane order. The desk says European defence should rise on Middle East de-escalation because it eases fiscal concerns. Valuations and positioning are both at the lows, with the GS European Defence basket hedge-fund long/short crowding ratio at about 0.7x, below its historical 10th percentile and down from about 3.0x in early 2024.

Prysmian rose 4% after beat-and-raise results. EBITDA beat by 7%, driven by a 20% beat in Electrification. Transmission was a small beat, Digital Solutions (fibre) missed slightly on light revenue, and Power Grid missed on margins. Quarterly FCF was light but the FY FCF guide was raised. EBITDA guidance was raised to a 3.1bn midpoint, implying about 6% upgrades to consensus.

On the Prysmian call management said Q4 margins will improve over Q3 and was upbeat on fibre and Electrification profitability. Bulls see room for further upgrades and say Digital Solutions is early in its cycle. The stock has been more de-risked than other electrical names.

Autos are in a possible Q4 squeeze: Stellantis (STLAM) rose 15% yesterday, Renault 7% and VW 2% today. VW's CFO said higher EV sales will weigh on margins in Q4 and into 2027. No one is embracing the rally, but it is hard to press shorts into year end now that 2027 estimate cuts are materialising.

Trucks and machinery had another day of negative news, with engcon and Knorr-Bremse (KBX) missing. IMI was the exception, citing strength in transport. Incoming client feedback mostly defends KBX (temporary order weakness, prudent project selectivity) and favours fading the truck OEMs, Traton and Volvo B in particular.

Epiroc has faded about 4% since its print. Christian (GS) sees the weakness as a buying opportunity given improving execution despite order slippage and equipment delivery delays. On the call management cited efficiencies in tools and attachments, very strong underground mining demand with a robust pipeline, and gold customers unfazed by the lower gold price.

European pulp and paper is under pressure again after a UPM miss and Smurfit Westrock down 5%. Gabriel (GS) calls the SW print weak but the 2027 outlook promising. Management said North American volumes recover in November and expects Europe to stay more rational than feared.

MTU Aero reported in-line Q3 EBIT (a 1% miss, weak OEM, strong commercial MRO) and a very strong FCF of 172m vs consensus 109m. Spares and MRO guidance were raised (up mid-teens vs low to mid-teens). The cash flow guide was narrowed to 55-60% of net income from 50-60%, with consensus at 54%.

Knorr-Bremse pre-released on weak rail vehicle systems (RVS) orders, blamed on project-driven fluctuations. It expects Q4 order intake of EUR 1.2bn vs consensus EUR 1.14bn. Q3 EBIT missed by 1.5%. GS analysts expect minor low-single-digit downgrades and see a negative read-across to rail OEMs Alstom and Siemens.

Renault Q3 sales beat by 2% and guidance was maintained at a margin around 5.5% with slight 2H improvement. Consensus models 5.1% in 2H vs 5.2% in 1H. Inventory is guided toward the lower end of 525-550k units, and the European orderbook is about 2 months of sales (2.1 at end of Q2). Client feedback remains very cautious.

Air Liquide Q3 comparable sales growth was +3% vs consensus +2.8%. Electronics accelerated and industrial merchant broadened, with US pricing of 6.5%. EMEA and Large Industries were soft and Healthcare decelerated. Management expects Q4 growth similar to Q3.

Volkswagen missed Q3 on VW Brand margins of 2.1% vs consensus 3.1%. Auto cash flow was slightly ahead. Guidance is unchanged after the recent cut. The desk says VW compares unflatteringly with Renault, Stellantis, Porsche and Mercedes and may struggle to join the 'no more warnings' auto bounce.

Catalysts the desk has a view on: Stora Enso on 3 Nov (Gabriel cautious on spinco valuation), Wartsila on 3 Nov (Daniela recently upgraded to Buy, sees CMD catalyst), FLSmidth on 17 Nov (Christian very bullish on FCF inflection and mid-term targets).
